before.beta: From the high pass south of the Birdwood Lakes, turn onto the northwest ridge and follow it up. The lower half is a loose, exposed scramble that most parties find stays near Class 3. Higher up the ridge steepens and narrows, with a short knife-edge and a few harder moves in the 5.4-5.5 range; rock quality is poor, so test every hold. Many parties carry a rope, a small rack and slings for the harder steps.

Begin next to Bubblenutz on its right and move rightward over a small roof onto a smooth slab and into a corner and up the face above. For the short corner, bring a few stoppers plus cams to roughly 2 inches.
Pick the left-hand flake, the one with the whitewashed tip, and climb the south face of the flake past its bolts to the top. To get off, scramble down and to the right.
Walk about fifty yards west from behind Hanging Gardens, then go up the slab that faces east, clipping its two bolts.
Start at the left end of the boulder's face and climb the face and arete, clipping two bolts, to the top. Get down with a single-rope rappel.

Start below the east end of the wall at a big boulder pile. Scramble right out of the ledge full of bushes to a large crack and a clear face. Climb the east face to the knife-edged top, then traverse left to get down.
Climb the face, clipping four bolts, to the stance on the shoulder over your head. After that you just walk off, which may feel like easy scrambling.

Climb the trough past a bolt to a ledge, then go up cracks and a dihedral to a small overhang. Pass the overhang on the left and climb the chimney to a ledge with a tree. The third pitch walks right into a gully to the foot of the friction slab, and the last climbs the face, clipping two bolts, to the top. The summit of the Head is a scramble from there.
Climb the east-facing side of the boulder, clipping two bolts, to the top. Descend with the same single-rope rappel used for Energizer.
Climb the offwidth crack that splits the face, then shift rightward to top out at a neighbor's anchor. Bring big cams, from a #2 up to a #6.
Gear to about two inches protects it. The moves low down are awkward, but overall it is a good climb for beginners.
Bring large protection, as the offwidth and chimney take gear up to about six inches.
From inside a large cave, the line moves onto overhanging rock with four bolts; carry a few natural pieces as well.
Gear needed runs to about two inches, with tiny pieces up to an inch especially useful. A single frustrating step reaches a tiny crystalline hole.
Protection is mostly nuts. The start and finish are inelegant, while the middle part of the route is enjoyable and exposed.
Gear needed up to about four inches. The crack is deceptive; the hardest moves are in the first twenty feet.
A full pitch with plenty of excitement near the top; bring cams in the number 2 to number 3 size for the crack. A short alternate start called Sidesaddle joins in.
Begin on the neighboring route, then after clipping its first bolt, veer rightward over a roof; a couple of small cams are worth bringing.
Begin next to the neighboring route, get by a decayed flake, then angle rightward along a dike to the face with two bolts; small TCUs are useful.
Large cams in the 3 and 4 sizes protect the crack.
Supplement the bolts with large nuts, sizes 4 to 5, and slings tied off around knobs.

Most parties stop after the first pitch, where the crack thins and you are pushed left to reach a far-off edge.

Gear to about 2 inches works, especially very small pieces under 1 inch.
